sections.html: Pterosturiosoma microps is one of the regularly imported Loricariidae from Peru, although not in bigger quantities. Even though it is more impressive in colour by its soft black-grey, it can still arouse enthusiasm by its remarkable appearance and its impressive but graceful fins. But its steady nursing is not quite easy.
The acclimatization probably seems to be the most problematic part, as it is difficult to get the fish used to food substitutes and/or they could possibly be pre-injured by the catch or transport.
As these catfish grow to a length of 20 cm, the tank should include 250 litres.

When the fish have got used to life in the aquarium and have recovered from the strains of transport, keeping them in a well-decorated and planted aquarium will be simple. Roots or the broad leaves of Vallisneria gigantea, for example, could be the preferred residences.

During the first time these fish persistently refuse to frequent a sandy or gravelled ground or other decoration materials, so they only eat what they find on still surfaces. Therefore it is recommended not to use substrate during quarantine, in order to get the animals into a good condition.
Unfortunately P. microps can only be kept with really peaceful fish that do not compete with it for food, because it has no self-assertion.
If you meet its requirements, P. microps can be an absolutely recommendable fish, but it surely is not an easy fish to keep.
